s: Enoch blesses the righteous and foretells that God will come down on Mount Sinai with his holy ones to judge the world. (Jude quotes this chapter.)
Look at the heavens: the sun, moon and stars keep their courses and never break God's order.
Look at the earth in winter: all the trees seem to wither, except fourteen that keep their leaves.
Look at the summer, when the sun burns and the earth grows hot.
All creation obeys God, but sinners have turned away from his law. The elect will inherit the earth, while sinners find no peace.
Two hundred angels, the Watchers, led by Semjaza, come down on Mount Hermon and swear an oath to take human wives.
The Watchers marry women and father giants, who devour the earth's food, then animals, then people.
Azazel teaches men to make weapons and women to use ornaments and make-up; other Watchers teach sorcery and astrology. Mankind cries out.
The archangels Michael, Uriel, Raphael and Gabriel see the bloodshed on earth and bring the people's cry before God.
God sends Uriel to warn Noah of the flood, Raphael to bind Azazel in darkness, and Michael to bind the Watchers until the judgment.
God promises to open the storehouses of blessing for the earth after it has been cleansed.
Enoch, hidden with the angels, is sent to tell the Watchers they will have no peace or forgiveness.
Enoch tells Azazel his sentence. The frightened Watchers ask him to write a petition for them, and he falls asleep and has a vision.
Enoch is taken up into heaven and sees God's great throne, surrounded by fire, and the Great Glory seated on it.
God tells Enoch that the Watchers left heaven to defile themselves, and that the spirits of the giants will become evil spirits on the earth.
The evil spirits will do harm until the judgment. The Watchers will have no peace.
Enoch begins his journeys. He is taken to places of fire and darkness, to the mountains, the great rivers and the ends of the earth.
Enoch sees the storehouses of the winds, the foundations of the earth, seven mountains of precious stones, and a prison for disobedient stars.
Uriel shows Enoch the place where the fallen angels will be held until the great judgment.
The names and tasks of the seven holy archangels.
Enoch sees a horrible place of fire where stars that broke God's commands are bound, and the prison of the angels.
Enoch sees the hollow places where the souls of the dead wait for judgment, divided between the righteous and sinners.
Enoch sees a fire in the west that pursues all the lights of heaven.
Enoch sees seven mountains, the middle one like God's throne, and a tree of wonderful fragrance.
The fragrant tree will be given to the righteous after the judgment, and its fruit will be food for the elect.
Enoch is taken to the middle of the earth and sees a holy mountain, Jerusalem, with a deep valley beside it.
The cursed valley is where those who blaspheme God will be gathered for judgment.
Enoch travels east into the desert and sees trees and water.
Further east, Enoch sees trees of fragrant spices.
Enoch sees valleys of water and trees of cinnamon and other spices.
Enoch sees mountains with trees giving nectar and sweet-smelling resins.
Enoch comes to the garden of righteousness and sees the tree of wisdom from which Adam and Eve ate.
At the ends of the earth Enoch sees great beasts and birds, and the gates from which the stars come out.
In the north, Enoch sees the gates of the winds that bring cold, frost, snow and rain.
In the west, Enoch sees three more gates of heaven.
In the south, Enoch sees three gates of the winds. He blesses God for all his works.
The Book of Parables begins: Enoch's second vision, a vision of wisdom for those who live on the earth.
The first parable. When the Righteous One appears, sinners will be judged and driven from the earth.
Enoch is carried to heaven and sees the dwellings of the righteous with the angels, and the Elect One under the wings of the Lord of Spirits.
Enoch sees countless angels before God, and four archangels who praise God, intercede and drive away the accusers.
Enoch sees the secrets of heaven: the dwellings of the elect, the storehouses of the winds, the courses of the sun and moon.
Wisdom found no home on earth and returned to heaven, but wickedness found a home among men.
Enoch sees lightning and the stars, called by name and weighed in righteous balance.
Some stars become lightning and cannot lose their form.
The second parable. The Elect One will sit on the throne of glory, and heaven and earth will be made new.
Enoch sees the Head of Days, white as wool, and with him one like a son of man, who will cast down kings and the mighty.
The prayers and blood of the righteous rise to God, and the books of the living are opened before the Head of Days.
Before the sun and stars were made, the Son of Man was named before the Lord of Spirits. He will be a staff for the righteous and a light to the nations.
Wisdom pours out like water before the Elect One, in whom dwells the spirit of wisdom and understanding.
The holy and elect will be glorified on the day of judgment, and sinners will be given the chance to repent.
The earth and Sheol will give back their dead, and the Elect One will choose the righteous.
Enoch sees mountains of metal that will melt before the Elect One. No gold or iron will save anyone on that day.
Enoch sees a deep valley where the angels of punishment prepare chains for the kings of the earth.
Enoch sees a valley of burning fire into which the hosts of Azazel will be thrown. The flood is foretold.
God swears never again to destroy all who dwell on the earth, and the Elect One will judge Azazel and his hosts.
The angels of punishment go out with chains. The Parthians and Medes will march on the holy land but will not take it.
Enoch sees chariots of men coming on the winds from east and west, and the whole earth praises God.
The third parable, on the righteous and elect: they will live in the light of the sun and in eternal life.
Enoch sees the secrets of the lightning and thunder.
Noah's vision of God's throne shaking. Behemoth and Leviathan are named, and the angel explains the secrets of the winds and waters.
The angels measure out the place of the righteous. The Elect One is set on the throne of glory and judges the deeds of the holy.
The kings and the mighty see the Son of Man on the throne of his glory and are seized with terror. The righteous will dine with him for ever.
The kings and the mighty beg for a little rest to repent and confess, but their time has passed and they are driven into darkness.
Enoch sees the angels who came down to earth and taught men secrets.
Noah sees the earth tilting and cries to his grandfather Enoch, who tells him the flood is coming and that he will be saved.
The angels of the waters are ready to release the flood.
God tells Noah that his family will be kept safe. The fallen angels are imprisoned in a valley of fire and water.
Michael and Raphael are shaken by the severity of the judgment on the fallen angels.
The names of the fallen angels and their crimes. The secret oath that holds creation in order. The Son of Man sits on the throne of his glory.
Enoch is taken up to heaven during his lifetime, to the presence of the Son of Man and the Lord of Spirits.
Enoch's spirit rises to the heaven of heavens and sees the house of fire, the angels and the Head of Days, and an angel greets him as a son of man born to righteousness.
The Book of the Luminaries begins. Uriel shows Enoch the laws of the sun, its six gates and the length of days through the year.
The laws of the moon, its phases and its light.
The moon's monthly course and a year of 364 days.
The leaders of the stars and the twelve gates of the winds.
The twelve gates from which the winds go out, bringing blessing or harm.
The four quarters of the earth, seven great mountains, seven rivers and seven islands.
The names of the sun and moon and the waxing and waning of the moon.
Enoch summarises the laws of the stars for his son Methuselah.
In the last days of sinners the seasons will be shortened and the stars will go astray.
Enoch reads the heavenly tablets with all the deeds of men, and he is returned to earth for a year to teach his children.
Enoch tells Methuselah to keep the books and to preserve the true calendar, and he describes the leaders of the seasons.
The Book of Dream Visions begins. In a first dream, Enoch sees the earth swallowed in a great abyss, and his grandfather tells him to pray.
Enoch's prayer that God will spare a remnant on the earth.
The second dream, the Animal Apocalypse, begins: Adam is a white bull, and Cain and Abel are bulls.
A star falls from heaven and then many stars, which become bulls with the cattle: the fall of the Watchers.
The giants are born, and the earth is filled with violence.
The angels bind the fallen stars and throw them into the abyss.
The history of Israel in animals: Noah, the flood, the patriarchs, Moses and the Exodus, the judges, the kings, the destruction of Jerusalem. The sheep go astray and are given to shepherds.
Seventy shepherds rule the sheep and destroy many of them. A great horn rises, the sheep are judged, a new house is built, and a white bull, the Messiah, is born.
Enoch calls his children and urges them to love righteousness. The Apocalypse of Weeks begins.
Enoch's letter to all his children and to the future generations who will keep righteousness.
The Apocalypse of Weeks: history in ten weeks, from Enoch himself to the final judgment and the new heaven.
Love righteousness and walk in it. Woes on those who build their houses with sin.
Enoch weeps over sinners and pronounces woes on those who repay their neighbour with evil.
The righteous will triumph over sinners. Woes on the rich and the oppressors.
Sinners will be put to shame on the day of judgment. Their wealth will not save them.
Sin was not sent upon the earth but created by man. Every deed is recorded in heaven.
Woes on the godless, on false witnesses and on those who change the words of truth.
In those days fathers and sons will fall together, and the righteous will be guarded by the angels.
Look at the heavens and the sea: they fear God. Sinners do not.
When God brings fire upon them, sinners will have no escape. The righteous should not grieve if their souls go down to Sheol in sorrow.
The souls of the righteous who died will live and rejoice. The souls of sinners will go down into torment.
The angels remember the righteous before God. They will shine like the lights of heaven.
God will send his word to the children of the earth, and he and his Son will dwell with the righteous for ever.
Noah is born with a body as white as snow and eyes like the sun. Lamech is afraid, and Methuselah goes to ask Enoch.
Enoch explains that the child will be saved from the flood, and tells Lamech to name him Noah.
A last book of Enoch: the reward of the humble righteous, who will shine in light, and the punishment of sinners in fire.
i: 1 Enoch is a collection of five books written by Jewish authors between about 300 BC and the time of Christ, all in the name of Enoch, the man who “walked with God, and was seen no more” (Genesis 5:24). Copies in Aramaic were found among the Dead Sea Scrolls. Only the Ethiopian Church kept the whole book, in Ge’ez, and only she reads it as Scripture.

What to expect: chapters 1 to 36 tell how the Watchers, angels who came down and took human wives, taught mankind sin and fathered the giants, and how Enoch is carried through heaven, earth and the underworld. Chapters 37 to 71, the Parables, speak of a heavenly “Son of Man” and “Elect One” who will judge the world. Chapters 72 to 82 are a book of astronomy and the calendar; 83 to 90 are dream visions that retell Israel’s history with animals; 91 to 108 are Enoch’s letter and warnings to his children.

It matters for Christians because it shaped the language of the New Testament. Saint Jude quotes it word for word (Jude 14-15: “Behold, the Lord comes with thousands of his saints”), and its picture of the Son of Man helps explain the title Jesus gave himself. The Catholic Church does not count it among the books of the Bible.

92: In older English “conversation” meant way of life and conduct, not talk.
